name: I Boot Right
purpose: Play action off the sweep look. Two receivers to the flanker side and a quarterback with the whole edge to himself. Run first, throw second.

LE.rule: Block down inside and sell the run. This has to look exactly like the sweep going the other way.

LT.rule: The tackle is on your inside shoulder. Block him down and seal him inside — that is what opens the hole.

LG.rule: Nobody is over you. Help the center on the nose and drive him away from the boot.

C.rule: Block the nose back toward the boot side. Nobody chases through the middle.

RG.rule: PULL LEFT and run the sweep path to sell the fake. You are a decoy — take a linebacker with you.

RT.rule: Hinge and protect the boot side. Nobody comes free outside you — the quarterback is alone back there.

RE.rule: Engage the end over you for a count, then release and settle at eight yards on the boot side.

Z.rule: Run to the flat at four yards and stay in front of the quarterback. You are the easy throw.

QB.rule: Fake the sweep with both hands, hide the ball on your back hip, and get to the edge. Run it if it is open. Only throw if a defender comes up to take you.

FB.rule: Run the sweep path away from the boot and block whatever shows. Sell it.

TB.rule: Run the full sweep path away from the boot with your arms tucked like you have the ball. Sell it all the way to the sideline.

coaching_points: Our ends must engage their end before releasing — sell the run first, then get out.
Run first. At this age the quarterback usually walks into ten yards before anyone finds him.
No blitzing is allowed for 8- and 9-year-olds, so the quarterback has time. Teach him to be patient and look up.
One throw, then tuck it. No scrambling backwards, ever.
